newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal's July-December trade gap up 14.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's July-December trade gap up 14.2 pct.

text.p: Nepal's trade deficit surged 14.2 percent to 24.57 billion rupees in the first five months of fiscal 1996/97 ending mid-July, from 21.52 billion rupees in the same year-ago period, officials said on Thursday.
Exports rose 27.6 percent to 9.13 billion rupees, while imports climbed 17.5 percent to 33.7 billion rupees, the Himalayan kingdom's central bank said on Thursday.
"We want to send our rugs to the United States and penetrate into the European market for garments," a senior official of the Commerce Ministry told Reuters.

Nepal Rastra Bank said the export of hand-knotted woollen carpets and ready made garments, totalled 4.04 billion rupees and 2.07 billion rupees respectively. These are Nepal's two principal items of exports.
The export of carpets and garments increased 26.2 percent and 44.2 percent respectively over the same period in the previous year.
The Nepali government recently announced a package to boost exports, focussing on diversifying traditional markets for these main products of exports.

Germany is the largest buyer of Nepali carpets, taking exports worth 8.16 billion rupees in 1995/96, while more than 90 percent of readymade garments, worth 5.36 billion rupees, were exported to the United States.
